requirement: Materialize a mapping of relative paths to text inside a fresh temporary directory, run a build callback there and return its bytes, always deleting the directory even when the build fails, and refusing paths that would escape the directory.
skeleton: workspace context manager wrapping TemporaryDirectory with prefix validation, and render_bundle writing files with parent creation and an escape check before calling build.
caption: Scratch build directories with the standard-library tempfile module and pathlib. workspace(prefix="build-") is a contextlib.contextmanager that raises ValueError saying the prefix must be a non-empty name without slashes, then enters tempfile.TemporaryDirectory with that prefix and yields its path, so the directory and everything in it are deleted when the block exits for any reason. render_bundle(files, build) opens a workspace, resolves its root, and for each relative path resolves the target inside it; a target that is not relative to the root, such as one reached through .., raises ValueError naming the path that escapes the workspace before anything is written. Otherwise it creates missing parent directories with mkdir using parents and exist_ok and writes the text as UTF-8. It returns whatever build returns when called with the workspace path. The fixture asserts that a nested src/pkg/main.txt is readable by the build, that the root name starts with build- and is gone afterwards, that the root is also gone after the build raises RuntimeError, that ../escape-111.txt raises ValueError and never appears in the system temporary directory, and that the prefix a/b raises ValueError.

constraints: The workspace directory is deleted after success and after failure
Workspace names start with build- by default
Nested relative paths get their parent directories created
Paths escaping the workspace raise ValueError
Prefixes that are empty or contain slashes raise ValueError

rationale.teaches: TemporaryDirectory inside a contextmanager for guaranteed cleanup, with resolve and is_relative_to guarding writes.
rationale.why: Hand-rolled temp dirs leak on errors and naive joins let a relative path write outside the sandbox, and neither shows up unless the test checks the filesystem after the call.

ops.docstring: Run a build step inside a scratch directory that is always removed afterwards.

ops.stmt: from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator, Mapping

candidates.why_wrong: Paths with .. are written wherever they resolve, outside the workspace.
mkdtemp creates the directory but nothing deletes it, so every build leaks its workspace.
The default prefix is bundle-, so workspaces are not named build-.
The escape check is inverted, so every legitimate path is rejected.
mkdir without parents fails with FileNotFoundError for nested paths.
